cross_module_architecture.dimension_character: The import graph has two real cycles and a small number of very high fan-in hubs, while the largest package is a flat grab bag of unrelated concerns. A developer cannot rely on dependency direction to tell them what may change independently.
cross_module_architecture.score_rationale: domain/models.py is now a re-export facade over seven aggregate modules; services/orchestration and services/host are capability subpackages.

high_level_elegance.dimension_character: Ownership is blurred because the codebase contains two generations of the optimizer and a CLI that is also a UI layer. A new engineer would struggle to say which module owns orchestration, which owns presentation, and which is dead legacy.
high_level_elegance.score_rationale: One workflow service, one host lifecycle module and capability subpackages replace the duplicated legacy and flat-service ownership.

convention_outlier.dimension_character: File and symbol naming follows one convention almost everywhere, so navigation by name is reliable. The outliers are not lexical but structural: type strategy, output mechanism and test layout change by directory without an explicit rule.
convention_outlier.score_rationale: Unit/integration markers and the documented type strategy make the two test roots and dataclass/Pydantic split explicit.

error_consistency.dimension_character: Error handling is defensive almost everywhere: broad catches and silent passes keep long-running optimization loops alive, but they also hide the cause and make failure modes depend on the call site. Predictability is low at module boundaries.
error_consistency.score_rationale: 128 silent catches log through best_effort; API 500s go through one _internal_error/exception handler.

naming_quality.dimension_character: Names usually predict behavior and the domain vocabulary is coherent, which is the main strength. The friction comes from duplicated type names across generations and from overloaded workflow verbs in the CLI, where 'optimize' and 'auto' mean both the command and the internal routine.
naming_quality.score_rationale: Legacy duplicate state is gone; internal CLI workflow helpers were renamed by responsibility.

abstraction_fitness.dimension_character: Most abstractions are direct domain helpers, but the codebase also carries a layer of adapter dicts and conversion wrappers that exist only to move data between representations. The cost is paid at every boundary, especially around settings and API serialization.
abstraction_fitness.score_rationale: AdvancedSettings, build_optimizer and Pydantic model_validate replace the main implicit dict/wrapper boundaries.

dependency_health.dimension_character: The dependency set is small and mostly current, with clear roles for the CLI, API and HTTP layers. The main drag is the two cycles plus a legacy GPU helper whose maintenance status is poor.
dependency_health.score_rationale: GPUtil and both cycles are gone; requirements.txt mirrors pyproject and uv.lock pins 63 packages.

low_level_elegance.dimension_character: At the helper level the code is direct and readable, but the large orchestration functions accumulate loading, benchmarking, quality checks, persistence and rendering in a single body. A reader must hold many side effects in mind at once.
low_level_elegance.score_rationale: Host lifecycle and optimizer composition moved out of the 5.7k-LOC CLI module; silent catches are logged.

mid_level_elegance.dimension_character: Module boundaries exist, but the data that crosses them is mostly raw dictionaries and tuples. Handoffs work, yet each layer must re-interpret the same keys, which makes integration seams fragile and duplicates policy.
mid_level_elegance.score_rationale: CLI/API/auto-run compose through one workflow/settings boundary; config detail has one presenter.

test_strategy.dimension_character: Test coverage is broad and the suite is fast, so developers get real feedback. The gaps are structural: the legacy engine/checkpoint path is untested, and the two-root layout makes it unclear which tests are the canonical regression suite.
test_strategy.score_rationale: 1508 tests pass; MockTransport contract tests and unit/integration markers were added.

api_surface_coherence.dimension_character: The API is broad and mostly REST-shaped, but its response contracts are inconsistent: some endpoints are typed, most are not. A client developer cannot rely on the generated schema or on a single error envelope.
api_surface_coherence.score_rationale: Core endpoints have response models, one error boundary, typed converters and supported include_router registration.

authorization_consistency.dimension_character: Authorization is uniformly absent rather than inconsistently applied: the app is a localhost tool, and every route trusts the local caller. Within that model the behavior is predictable, but the trust boundary is implicit and not documented at the API surface.
authorization_consistency.score_rationale: Remote binds require LM_OPTIMIZER_API_TOKEN; mutating non-loopback requests need X-API-Token.

ai_generated_debt.dimension_character: The code does not read like unedited generated output: comments are sparse and names are domain-specific. The debt is behavioral rather than cosmetic, mostly defensive exception handling and leftover console output in service paths.
ai_generated_debt.score_rationale: Service prints are gone, 128 silent catches log, and long-function docstrings now list side effects.

incomplete_migration.dimension_character: A full legacy stack coexists with the new one, and the migration is documented but not finished. Active modules still reach into the old client and engine, so the boundary between current and retired code is not real.
incomplete_migration.score_rationale: Legacy engine/web/checkpoint/runner are deleted; discovery now uses the service client and api/client is documented as test-only.

package_organization.dimension_character: The core packages are named by capability and are easy to navigate. The degradation is at the edges: a flat services grab bag, ad-hoc root scripts and a tools directory that mixes durable utilities with campaign leftovers.
package_organization.score_rationale: Domain aggregates, orchestration and host are now purpose-named packages; services/ is materially less flat.

initialization_coupling.dimension_character: Boot order matters more than it should: importing a module can create directories, register routes or capture the config snapshot. Global mutable state in the API layer further couples requests to process history.
initialization_coupling.score_rationale: Route table registration is two include_router calls; logging setup is entrypoint-only; current-run globals remain.

design_coherence.dimension_character: Design decisions are locally reasonable but globally inconsistent: the active optimizer has a clear phase pipeline, while the CLI and the legacy stack duplicate orchestration. Large functions accumulate multiple responsibilities instead of composing collaborators.
design_coherence.score_rationale: One optimizer/workflow/checkpoint path; the remaining drag is the CLI command bodies and _test_config.

contract_coherence.dimension_character: Contracts are mostly honest at the dataclass level, but function-level contracts drift at the edges: None signals multiple outcomes, dict returns vary, and docstrings omit failure paths. A developer often has to read the body to know what a call can produce.
contract_coherence.score_rationale: Client/benchmark/repository error contracts and failed-report semantics are documented; dict-shaped returns remain.

logic_clarity.dimension_character: Small functions are easy to trace, but the long orchestration bodies require holding several concurrent states (loaded model, current config, retry budget, report data). The logic is not wrong, but it is not always locally obvious what the success condition is.
logic_clarity.score_rationale: classify_run is the single success predicate; 46 no-await handlers became sync; retry branches remain in host loading.

type_safety.dimension_character: Type annotations are trustworthy in the domain dataclasses and Pydantic schemas, but large parts of the service and CLI surface are untyped or typed as dict/Any. A developer cannot rely on annotations to describe runtime behavior across boundaries.
type_safety.score_rationale: AdvancedSettings, DefaultsDocument and annotated public entrypoints improve the boundary; most helpers remain untyped.

add.description: backends/base.py defines BackendClient and assert_conforms, and OllamaClient implements the seam; backend-specific code is not spread through the domain.
web_main.py launches api.main:app, and ui/web.py is explicitly marked as deprecated reference code, so the current entrypoint is unambiguous.
The deprecated ui/web.py docstring names api.main:app as authoritative, which prevents a new engineer from wiring the wrong app.
OptimizationPhase/OptimizationStage enumerate the pipeline stages instead of relying on implicit string flow, which gives the orchestration a readable spine.
1,666 detected names across all packages use snake_case, so lexical convention is not a source of friction.
Most test modules are named after the production module they cover, which makes coverage discovery predictable.
BenchmarkService records success=False and an error per case instead of aborting the whole sweep, which keeps one bad prompt from losing a run.
Cancellation paths explicitly checkpoint state before unwinding, preserving recoverability across failures.
Terms such as run, configuration, phase, winner and ladder are used consistently across CLI, API and services, so domain names transfer between layers.
The BackendClient protocol is implemented by OllamaClient and exercised by conformance checks, so the abstraction has more than one consumer.
Functions such as parse_phase_skips and compose_granular_skips encode real skip semantics rather than forwarding arguments.
One HTTP client (httpx), one settings stack (pydantic-settings) and one CLI/UI stack (Typer/Rich + FastAPI) avoid duplicate-purpose libraries.
Helpers such as _looks_incomplete, _sample_mem and _extract_mtp_metrics are short, side-effect-light and easy to test.
The optimizer exposes ordered phases and skip names, so the CLI/API handoff for phase control is at least named and testable.
About 1,490 tests run in roughly five minutes, covering phases, scoring, persistence and CLI/UI parity.

add.header: Targeted regression tests for live findings
add.description: Load-response loss, echo-probe cleanup and context-speed ladder retries each gained a dedicated test after being found live.
Run, settings, compare, sandbox and judge endpoints use Pydantic response models, giving the most important payloads a stable schema.
The web UI binds 127.0.0.1 by default and CORS allows only localhost origins, reducing accidental network exposure.
The 2.5% comment ratio and short docstrings avoid restating code; comments generally explain constraints or intent.
web_main.py launches api.main:app and the deprecated module points to it, so the target of the migration is unambiguous.
domain, storage, backends, benchmark and scoring are named by responsibility, so the main layout is self-explanatory.
pydantic-settings provides one typed config object with environment support, avoiding scattered os.environ reads in most modules.
The FastAPI app uses a lifespan context for startup/shutdown work, giving a clear place for future initialization.
AdaptiveOptimizer runs named phases (speed, context speed, quality, recovery, validation) with explicit skip handling, which is a coherent orchestration spine.
Core domain dataclasses expose to_dict/from_dict pairs and are exercised by round-trip tests, giving persistence a reliable contract.
CLI and API helpers commonly validate inputs and return/raise early, keeping the happy path visible in short functions.
Domain dataclasses and Pydantic schemas type the main entities (runs, configs, metrics, requests), giving the persistence and HTTP layers a reliable core.
